author: Autodesk
description: Creates a landscape of rolling hills and puts a forest of simple cartoony trees into the valleys of that landscape.
documentation:
Creates a landscape of rolling hills and puts a forest of simple cartoony trees into the valleys of that landscape.

The terrain is not the purpose of this graph, but the terrain is composed of a mesh plane, a scaled noise field, and a displace points. 

## Scatter points driven by weights

Scatter points here is driven by weights, and the weights control where scattering takes place. 

Scatter points is intended to be augmented by use-case specific visual programming. One of those ways is using the “interpreted auto port” of weights, where scattering can be controlled like a mask with a variety of kinds of data. Interpreted auto ports can take in raw arrays of data (as we are doing here), and can also take a variety of other data types including fields or names of properties. 

## Weights by elevation

This is the important compound in this graph. This is a simple compound which maps an F-Curve onto a Y gradient of the terrain, letting users control the falloff upward using the natural control of an f-curve in the zero to one range. 

The way it accomplishes is by first normalizing the positions into a zero-one range in their bounding box. A change range which maps the min and max to zero and one does this. After that an f-curve is applied to the normalized positions, giving users an f-curve in the zero-one range. The input X value is the elevation, and the output Y value is the amount of scattering. The default curve has a sharp cutoff at a middle-elevation, creating bare hills and richly populated valleys. 

## Creating trees and instances

A small compound creates an array of simple tree out of a sphere and some random deformation. It does this in a for-each loop, which will generate the trees in parallel and output an array. These will be selected from randomly and use different seeds to create some variation. Create instances is configured to select randomly from the tree shapes. 

This tree could be replaced by render archive instances to use full renderable assets instead of dummy geometry.  

## Point manipulations

After that, scale points, randomize point scale, and randomize point rotation are used in straightforward ways to add randomness.

metadata.description: Creates a landscape of rolling hills and puts a forest of simple cartoony trees into the valleys of that landscape.

_notes.text: Scatter points is set to use Blue Noise (meaning space points roughly evenly) and by radius (meaning the control is the avoidance radius).
The points are scaled to a single size (using type wrangling to set the scale to a single float).  After that, the scales and rotations are randomized.
***set_geo_property_reference*** allows you to set a material attribute with a *geo_property*.  In this case the materials *base_color* is reading the *point_color* from the geometry.

_backdrops.title: Assign a shader to the instances

_notes.text:
# weights

This compound creates per-point weights by mapping an f-curve from the highest to the lowest point. 

It does this by getting the positions of the mesh (terrain) and remapping them to a 0-1 range.  The height (y-axis) is then retrieved and an fCurve applied.

# displace

This compound creates a terrain by displacing a plane with a field.

The ***fractal_turbulence_field*** generates a vector field.  The ***vector_to_color*** compound normalizes the field, and fits the output to a <0,0,0> to <1,1,1> range.

The y-component of the field is sampled and then used in a ***get_from_interpolated_array*** to sample from a 2 color array.  This will generate a ramp to be used for color.
The y-component is taken from the positions and remapped to a 0.2 - 1 range.  This is then multiplied with the color.
***set_geo_property_reference*** is the compound that allows the material to use a *geo_property* as an input.
Preparing the meshes that will make up the trees - the cubes are the trunks and the spheres will represent the leaves.

These fields will be used to displace each tree as we go around the loop.  The ***bitwise_xor*** compounds are used to generate a unique seed for the displacements using the current index of the loop.
But default, ***displace_points*** displaces a mesh along it's normals if they exist.  In this case we are replacing that with a generated vector.
The ***random_value*** compound generates a random color per "leaves" mesh.  To change the colors, modify the *min* and *max* values.
